A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

happiness, as defined by the hedonic approach to well being, has its roots in the biological and genetic systems and is relatively stable over time and across cultures, while meaning and self realization, as defined by eudaimonic approaches to well being, have roots in the sociocultural system and are less stable.

the eudaimonia approach has provided us with a better understanding of the meaning of well being and the conditions under which people can experience optimal experience and functioning, whereas the hedonic approach has provided us more precise measures for the assessment of happiness.
well being is a multidimensional, multilevel phenomenon that is best understood by examining the interaction among individual characteristics, social contexts, and the cultural environment.
